page: Microsoft Azure E4_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, with instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and VNNI supported.

The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio typical of memory-intensive tiers. In synthetic memory testing, the instance registers a PassMark memory score of 2,211.77, along with uncached large-block read bandwidth of 23.02 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 18.0 GB/sec. The instance includes no local storage, requiring persistent workloads to rely exclusively on network-attached Azure managed disks, and it does not include hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal modest processing throughput relative to modern high-density compute nodes. The E4_v4 achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1,226.0 and a multi-core score of 2,742.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 4,339.65. Synthetic workload metrics demonstrate Redis SET operations at 3.56 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 3.79 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression registers in the average bracket at 9.19 GB/sec, though heavily parallelized and compute-bound tasks exhibit lower comparative efficiency.

Given its high RAM-to-vCPU ratio and moderate compute capacity, the E4_v4 serves as a balanced, cost-effective resource tier for memory-centric applications that do not demand extreme raw processing power. Practical deployments include intermediate relational database hosting, in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, lightweight enterprise applications, and staging environments for memory-bound services.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system incorporates 2 physical cores with hyperthreading and 35 MB of L3 cache, supporting AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage solutions. Benchmark assessments place its processing capability in lower-to-moderate tiers, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,742.0 and a PassMark memory score of 2,211.77. In-memory operations reach 3.56 million Redis SET operations per second. The E4_v4 delivers balanced resource allocation without premium compute overhead, making it best suited for moderate relational databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring high memory density over raw computational speed.
